content.text:
I’m oriented on the project.

QuoteCraft is an agentic solution for Atira’s “RFQ to Bid” challenge:

- Four model-directed browser agents investigate the tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mail in parallel.
- Relevant pages become typed evidence in a shared case file.
- A deterministic `Decimal` calculator applies the commercial rules.
- A final agent completes the bid form, retrieves the TAN from mail, and submits.

The architecture and usage are documented in [starter-kit/README.md](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/README.md) and the current handoff is in [PROJECT_STATUS.md](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/PROJECT_STATUS.md).

Key constraint: it must work on unseen/private layouts with no scenario-specific URLs, selectors, credentials, values, or scripted navigation. The model must choose research and navigation at runtime; deterministic code is intentionally limited to browser mechanics, evidence handling, and arithmetic.

Current state: the old hardcoded approach reportedly earned a strong public result but made zero model calls, so it was deliberately replaced. The current model-directed rebuild includes the core agent loop, evidence extraction, 29-rule calculator, submission flow, four-browser configuration, and substantial unit coverage.

Main remaining risks:

- Browser regression: the remote “Load more” collection test is currently failing.
- Question-dialog close state is also documented as unreliable.
- The multi-action submission patch under `tools/` is intentionally not yet applied.
- A public non-submitting end-to-end run and official challenge test still need validation.

I also checked the Entire history: 15 local checkpoints are present on `main`, including the agentic rewrite and test-suite additions. Entire’s remote history search is currently unavailable because this repository is not mirrored to its search service, but the local checkpoints and Brain facts were usable.

QuoteCraft is an agentic solution for Atira’s “RFQ to Bid” challenge:

- Four model-directed browser agents investigate the tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mail in parallel.
- Relevant pages become typed evidence in a shared case file.
- A deterministic `Decimal` calculator applies the commercial rules.
- A final agent completes the bid form, retrieves the TAN from mail, and submits.

| Part of QuoteCraft | Main code files | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Overall coordinator | [agent.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.py) | Reads the task, launches the four researcher agents, waits for evidence, calculates the bid, then starts submission. |
| Four browser researchers | [worker.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/worker.py) | Generic model-agent loop used for tender, supplier, ERP, and email sites. The model chooses actions and decides when a page is evidence. |
| Browser interaction | [browser_env.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/browser_env.py) | Converts webpages into accessible text/control descriptions; safely performs click, fill, select, search, page collection, frames, dialogs, and downloads. |
| Model calls | [llm.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/llm.py) | Calls the hosted Qwen model through Atira’s proxy, validates JSON replies, retries failures, and caps concurrency. |
| Shared evidence and facts | [casefile.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/casefile.py) | Stores filed pages, extracts structured tender/ERP/mail facts, merges them, and exposes unanswered research questions. |
| Commercial calculation | [calculator.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/calculator.py) | Pure deterministic `Decimal` bid calculation: material matching, prices, currencies, discounts, stock, delivery, fees, and rounding. |
| Bid entry, TAN, final submission | [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py) | Runs the tender-form clerk agent, asks the mail agent for a fresh TAN, validates form progress, and captures the receipt. |
| Challenge-run plumbing | [run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/run.py), [browsers.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/browsers.py), [models.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/models.py) | Reads the Atira run contract, connects to the supplied browsers, and provides model configuration. |
| Runtime configuration | [agent.json](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.json) | Declares the setup/run command, Qwen model, and the maximum four browsers. |
| Tests | [tests](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/tests) | Tests calculator rules, agent/submit plumbing, and browser edge cases using local HTML fixtures. |
| Local development helper | [local_run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/tools/local_run.py) | Runs the system locally against public challenge sites, typically without submitting. |

In short: `agent.py` orchestrates; `worker.py` thinks and researches; `browser_env.py` operates sites; `casefile.py` remembers evidence; `calculator.py` prices; and `submit.py` sends the bid.

I found and checked `maria/build` (the branch name is `maria`, not `mari`).

It is based on `7dce502`, with five Maria-specific commits:

- Faster navigation by disabling model thinking during navigation (`AGENT_THINK=1` re-enables it).
- More resilient mail-gate and extraction timeout handling.
- Retry support when fact extraction fails.
- Optional OpenAI provider for fact extraction via `EXTRACT_PROVIDER`.
- A new `tuning/replay_extraction.py` script for replaying saved evidence against different extraction models.

It changes seven files, primarily [llm.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/llm.py), [casefile.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/casefile.py), [worker.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/worker.py), and its own version of [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py).

Important: it cannot be cleanly merged into current `main` as-is.

- `starter-kit/casefile.py`: content conflict.
- `starter-kit/submit.py`: add/add conflict, because both `main` and Maria’s branch independently introduced a submission implementation.
- `main` also has six commits not present in Maria’s branch, including the newer calculator tests, local harness, performance fixes, and browser regression suite.

The branch’s own diff has no whitespace errors. It looks useful as a source of focused performance/reliability improvements, but its extraction/provider and submission changes need a deliberate merge rather than a blind merge.
